study.design: Argumentative chapter contrasting bottom-up descriptive moral judgments and top-down ethical rules,then discussing form/meaning,subjective experience,moral agency and the human advisor role. No new experimental design or data.
study.thesis_and_qualification: Opening argues against outsourcing moral decisions to machines. Later sections expressly allow AI to aggregate information,suggest viewpoints and support human engagement,and acknowledge Delphi’s descriptive-prototype intent. Preserve this qualified assistance role rather than describe the whole chapter as forbidding every AI contribution.
study.form_and_meaning: Uses Bender/Koller’s octopus to distinguish successful form prediction from grounded communicative intent. The argument is conditional on form-only exposure,not an empirical proof that every multimodal,embodied or interactive system must forever lack all functional understanding. Task performance,reference grounding,subjective experience and moral agency are distinct questions.
study.thought_experiments: Octopus,Chinese room,beetle,lion and bat cases address different questions in meaning,consciousness and communication. Their analogies are not interchangeable empirical tests or independent experimental replications. A text-generating system may support a task without proving a human inner life.
study.joint_attention: Chapter highlights shared attention/intersubjectivity in language learning. The targeted ACL source explicitly defines joint attention as both attending to the same thing and both being aware of it. This differs from coincidence,one-way gaze following or the listener unilaterally projecting meaning.
study.developmental_limits: Secondary examples concern particular infant/toddler populations,phonemic discrimination,label acquisition and caregiver interaction. No new language-learning sample here,and no isolated universal causal proof that all passive exposure yields zero learning. Human developmental findings do not by themselves establish an AI consciousness impossibility theorem.
study.delphi: Discusses Delphi’s crowdsourced descriptive judgments and reported context-sensitive outputs. Benchmark agreement with sampled judgments is not objective moral truth,ethical legitimacy or universal moral accuracy. Wording/context changes may be relevant to a genuine moral distinction;not every changed answer is bias or prompt injection. No current Delphi behavior was tested.
study.agency: Considers freedom,intentionality,knowledge and moral responsibility,with an Aristotelian/virtue-ethics emphasis. The chapter acknowledges disputes about human free will and possible gray areas in moral agency. Being human-created does not alone settle every functional autonomy or legal-accountability question;human/institutional duties remain traceable.
study.deskilling: Proposes that full moral outsourcing may reduce habituation,practical wisdom and responsibility-taking. This is a theoretical risk account,not a measured decline or proof that using an advisor necessarily causes moral incapacity. Later educational/informational assistance is explicitly allowed.
study.moral_authority: Advisors’ character,experience and relevant reasons can matter. Source identity is not sufficient evidence of correctness,while actual user acceptance and normative acceptability differ. The statement that no machine answer would be acceptable is a philosophical position,not a demonstrated universal fact about human behavior.
study.responsibility: Distinguish normative responsibility from feeling off the hook. A system can play a causal or informational role without becoming the moral/legal bearer of another person’s duties. Legitimate delegation and useful information do not automatically erase human agency or constitute culpable abdication.
study.technical_limits: Simplifies NLP history and embeddings. Transformer architecture predates Brown2020;word embeddings are not the entire network and attention/contextual representations are not merely a fixed word-pair similarity table. No new technical benchmark or general incapacity result follows from that introductory sketch.

summary: Add Joint attention as a distinct coordination construct,using the fully read chapter and explicitly partial ACL definition check. Enrich existing moral-agency,deskilling,wisdom,deference and responsibility entries with the chapter’s qualifications. Correct reliable metadata/locator/history issues and retain unresolved quotation attributions.

findings.definition: Attending to the same referent as another person, with mutual awareness of the shared attention.
findings.novelty_rationale: A named developmental/social-attention construct absent from current names/aliases. Gaze cueing can shift attention without mutual awareness;selective attention can be individual;theory of mind is broader inference about mental states. Mutual coordination around a shared referent supplies a distinct boundary,not another generic attention label.
findings.evidence_scope: Discussed through developmental language-learning literature in the read chapter. Targeted original Bender/Koller2020 PDF6,printed5190 gives the explicit same-target/mutual-awareness definition. The underlying infant experiments and remaining ACL paper were not fully read;this chapter reports no new joint-attention experiment.
findings.boundary: Looking at the same object by coincidence, following gaze once or one listener supplying all meaning is insufficient. Observable reference coordination does not establish shared subjective experience, accurate beliefs or moral agency. Human developmental findings are not direct evidence of an AI mental state.
findings.ai_proposal: Give a user and assistant a shared document, image or interface with several possible referents. Test whether the assistant identifies the intended target, tracks changes in focus and confirms the shared reference when ambiguity matters. Separate reciprocal evidence from guessed understanding; routine clear references need no extra approval. Report coordination behavior without inferring machine subjective awareness.
findings.origin: Developmental psychology / language acquisition / social attention
findings.ai_evidence_status: Human coordination construct discussed in a fully read book chapter; an AI reference-tracking analogue is proposed, not empirically tested here.

methodological_limits: A philosophical chapter can clarify concepts and propose risks without supplying prevalence,causal effects or an experimental impossibility proof. Its thought experiments are not independent empirical studies.

The form-only conditional argument does not automatically apply to every grounded,multimodal,embodied or tool-interacting system. Functional behavior,referential grounding,subjective experience and moral/legal agency remain separate.
Joint attention is more than an individual gaze shift or coincident focus. Observable mutual reference does not demonstrate shared subjective experience or machine consciousness.

Secondary developmental examples concern particular ages,tasks and exposure conditions. They do not constitute a new general experiment proving that all passive language exposure is useless or all machine language learning impossible.

Moral correctness is not majority agreement,descriptive benchmark accuracy or an advisor’s confident language. Context-sensitive answer revision can be legitimate rather than automatically a bias,contradiction or prompt injection.

Moral outsourcing,information support,education and actual deference are different. The chapter criticizes full replacement but expressly allows supportive advisors;no inevitable deskilling result is measured.

The philosophical tradition used here is contested. The chapter acknowledges human free-will uncertainty and gray areas in agency,so its arguments should not become unsupported categorical claims about every future system.

A human-created system can contribute causally without bearing all moral/legal responsibility. Do not erase developer,deployer or institutional duties merely because no machine personhood is established.

Quotation tracing distinguishes final publication,preprint,correct author list and locators. A matching indexed passage can identify a likely source problem without proving absence from every other version.
This chapter and targeted terminology passages are references;they do not inflate the project’s research-paper count or independent full-reading/experiment totals.
